title: Can Collagen Supplements Help Arthritis?
abstract: Can Collagen Supplements Help Arthritis? Scientists have identified 28 types of collagen, but four or five usually make it into dietary supplements. * Type II makes up about 90% of the collagen in cartilage. In studies, people with osteoarthritis (OA) were more likely to have high levels of this type of collagen. There are two main types of collagen dietary supplements:. * **Undenatured type II collagen** (UC-II). Collagen supplements have been investigated as treatment for a host of problems, including aging skin, wound healing, OA, RA, bone health (osteoporosis) and high cholesterol. A recent review and meta-analysis of 19 studies involving more than 1,000 people looked at collagen for skin health and wound healing and found excellent results for both. * An analysis of 41 animal and human studies, including 25 clinical trials, found that collagen benefited OA and aided cartilage repair, no matter what the dose, type or brand of collagen.
